reference_gaps.expected: OPT inlines fc1/fc2 on the decoder layer, so no module's *input* is the residual between the sublayers, and the norm that would carry it cannot be identified by name: OPT calls it `final_layer_norm`, which is also what the trunk calls the model's final norm, and `config.do_layer_norm_before` decides whether it runs before the MLP (opt-125m) or after it (opt-350m). interp-engine refuses rather than binding the wrong module on one of the two shapes; TransformerLens knows which from its own conversion

run.dtype_note: engines load the checkpoint's native dtype (dtype='auto'); SGLang serves bf16 only (float32 unsupported), so a float32-native model's SGLang cell is a cross-dtype fused case.
